Our Beirut Mixed Grill is one of our signature best-selling dishes- a rather large portion of charcoal grilled kofta, chicken shish tawouk, filet beef kebab - perfect for sharing for 2 people: 598,000vnd ($25)

Shisha - we use premium imported shisha tobacco - never fake, never with additives: Large size: 390,000 ($16)

Cocktails price ranges from 138,000 - 198,000vnd ($6-8)

Please note we do not charge 15% service charge, but rather it is VAT 10% (which is local tax) + 5% service charge normally on every bill which is given to all our staff as we notice a majority of customers do not leave tips in Vietnam.

Beirut_Saigon
Hello Annon1963, 

Wow, we are really sorry. We wish you had directly reported every single one of your complaints to our Manager so we would make sure you would be taken care of and given a bill refund immediately. 

Funny, I didn't see you write a review of any sort about Warda- one of our neighboring smaller scale competitors. 

Regardless, I would like to point out a few facts:

First off, we do not tolerate insults of any kind about our staff working at Beirut as majority of our team has been working with us for over 5 years and they have been working very hard to ensure quality service to all our happy customers. 

You mentioned you were "directed" to a table - without a reservation we may not be able to give out your preferred table or sofa-booth seating reserved for groups of 6-8 people. Our restaurant accommodates 150-200 people - we are generally busy on any given evening and majority of tables have been reserved in advance. 

Secondly, our belly dancers are certified professional belly dancers - they are not "eye candy lap dancers". Belly-dancing is a traditional form of dancing in the Middle-East and part of our much respected culture. Our belly-dancers add to the mysterious fun-filled ambience at Beirut Restaurant & Shisha Lounge. Single customers, families, couples, party groups have all appreciated our belly-dancers performances. 

Lastly, we serve 100% authentic middle-eastern and mediterranean cuisine, definitely one of the best and most authentic in town. Our head chef is from Beirut, Lebanon. Our prices are at the average mark and we guarantee 100% high quality in our food, drinks and shisha. 

Beirut is a place for people who wish to experience the real Middle-Eastern culture & foods and fun in an authentic Arabian inspired ambience. 

From the sounds of it - it seems you were searching for a really quiet and peaceful experience.
We do sincerely hope you enjoy the rest of your peace & quiet-searching time in Vietnam. 

Regards, 
Beirut

Good food, but terrible value
Jul 2016 • Friends
I tried Beirut with a friend. The restaurant was already here when I moved to Ho Chi Minh City six years ago. There is also a sister restaurant in Hanoi. They certainly know how to run a business.

The place is huge and includes tables, sofas, and cosy booths. It is what might have been a large warehouse. Do not expect chilly air conditioning, but they do a decent job with fans. 

I am not an expet in middle eastern cuisine. I can only say that we ordered an appetizer mix (mezza platter), grilled lamb and a kebab with mutton. Much more is available of course and the menu is fully illustrated. 

The mezza platter included hummus and a number of herbs and sauces (and two tiny falafels). It was good to go with the bread, but honestly not much to eat.

I and my friend enjoyed the main courses, my grilled lamb was excellent. 

However looking back, I can say thaat the value for money was terrible. The appetizer sampling platter cost 20 dollars (including 10% VAT and 5% service charge) and frankly there was really little to eat... Each main course was another 15-20 US dollars and was by no means a large dish... We spent 10 USD just for two bottle of imported water (local one not available). 

Overall the food was enjoyable (that's why I am leaving a generous 4 star rating), but I would not go back since with that kind of money I can find way better food for my tastes. Of course, if you really like kebabs and co. and if you do not mind the splurge, it can be worth for the nice ambience. 

A final note on the belly dancing show. I think it is at 8pm (I do not know whether every day, for sure it was on when we visited on a Saturday evening). I am not questioning the artistic value of the show, but it is very noisy... and you cannot escape it. So if you like this kind of noisy entertainment, it is probably a great addition to the dinner experience, For me, just one more reason not to go back.

Go for the Entertainment not the Food....
Mar 2016 • Business
We recently experienced an odd evening at Beirut Garden. We were taking clients out for the evening in Ho Chi Minh and had heard about a large Lebanese restaurant with a terrific belly dancing show in the Ben Nghe Ward (cool area in HCM with a variety of clubs and restaurants across from the Park Hyatt). We were surprised at the massive size of the place. It is open on one end with an arched glass roof atrium, colorful fabric hanging everywhere, and a huge stage with bar at the other end. In the middle are many tables and along one side are fabric draped booths with sofas. We knew we were in for an interesting evening when we attempted to order five different bottles of wine from their menu, none of which were in stock. I have to add that we were one of approximately 5 tables in the whole place at the time and it a was early in the evening. We finally settled on local beer. The same scenario held true for the food menu. Our first few selections were not available. We finally just asked what was available and ended up with the mixed grill (chicken, lamb, beef), Halloumi Cheese, eggplant rahib dip, and the stuffed grape leaf plate (dolmades). None of the food was particularly flavorful. It was, in fact, very bland. The evening did brighten up, though, as soon as the belly dancers took the stage. The dancers were very talented. They performed in front of a giant screen with colorful projections. The music was recorded, but very energetic and authentic. There is no question, the entertainment is the highlight of Beirut Garden. I would not rule out a re-visit but most likely just for drinks and the entertainment.

Jul 2014 • Business
First off, we did not eat dinner here, we had actually ended up eating dinner at another place nearby. But sometime after 9pm we heard this loud music that was neither local nor Western and, intrigued, went to go see what it is about. One of the people in our party said "it must be Beirut Garden, they have dancing after 9pm". What kind of dancing, we wondered? Let's go check it out. 

This is a large open restaurant with a long, wide bar below an expansive stage. They have some large booth seating along one of the walls but otherwise it's a lot of open tables in a very large open room. We had already eaten but the food we saw looked excellent, this is Lebanese food, not Vietnamese. 

We sat at a table and were quickly waited on where we ordered drinks and settled back to enjoy the show which had already started. The most amazing belly dancers start out on the stage and slowly but surely work their way down to the general dining area, stopping to dance for 30-60 seconds at each table. They do this for maybe 10-15 minutes and then go backstage to rest, change, and get ready for their next dance. The night we were there we got to enjoy three different dancers with short breaks between the dancers. Each dancer we got to see twice in different outfits and slightly different style of dancing. 

The belly dancers were truly incredibly, they put on a great performance, smiling and very engaging at every table they went to. They must have been very hot, sweaty, and tired but they really put on a great performance. 

All the while the restaurant staff were very attentive, constantly checking to see if we needed more drinks or were hungry for food. One of the managers (we think) came by at one point and introduced himself, shaking all of our hands and asking us what we thought, how did we like the place, anything they can improve, etc. 

All-in-all this was a great place to relax and next time will definitely try the food too. I would be comfortable bringing my family here, there were plenty of couples and larger parties here and the restaurant seems quite nice.

Tacky but fun
May 2013 • Couples
I went to Beirut last week and had a great time. Located off of Hai Ba Trung but can also be accessed from Cao Ba Quat. The place is large and was clearly decorated by someone who has a very limited sense of décor. However, I am personally ok with tacky if not a lot of money was spent and you can kind of tell that the owner had a relatively tight budget. That being said, it is not an eyesore and its open space looking out into the restaurant courtyard gives it an airy, open and relaxing atmosphere. Plus if you bring your putter you can practice on the astro turf carpeting.

The wine selection by the glass is paltry but the rose we ordered was quite good. One in our company had a Singaporean draft beer that he said was good and cold. We ordered an appetizer sampler and everything on it was delicious especially the hummus. We also ordered the artichoke app and as I consider myself something of an artichoke snob I was skeptical. But it was delicious, with just the right amount of garlic and lemon. Ebert & Siskel Two Thumbs Up for sure.

We ordered as entrees the lamb kebobs and grilled sausage. Both were very tasty although the pita underneath is a bit of overkill given how much unleavened bread one gets throughout the course of the meal. 

For dessert, we partook of the now obligatory waterpipe. The wait staff kept it lit and for they for the most part were attentive throughout the evening. One beef I do have in general with wait staff in Vietnam is that they tend to give you the menu and then stand by your table with pen and paper in hand patiently(?) waiting for you to give them your order. Maybe it's just me but I have an immediate flashback remembering to the time pressures one experiences as a young student taking a math test. The problem becomes if you ask them to come back, they rarely do unless you hunt them down or yell "em oi" to get their attention, which usually gets you a "oh, look it speaks" stare from the locals.

There was an elevator music band that sang the Stylistics and ABBA. It was pure cheese whiz but kind of added to the comfortable kitsch vibe of the place.

The tab was not too horrible but certainly not a basement bargain either. 

All in all, would I come back? Absolutely, it was fun, comfortable and relaxing. The food was solid with the highlight being the apps. I think it is a good place for two or three couples to go and enjoy a pleasant and different cuisine together.
